newsitem.title: FRANCE: French barley fails to react to Saudi tender.
newsitem.headline: French barley fails to react to Saudi tender.

text.p: French feed barley prices failed to react to Saudi Arabia's decision to seek 700,000 tonnes amid question marks over the European Union's likely response.
Rouen-delivered barley for May was quoted at 860 francs excluding carrying charges, unchanged from late on Thursday, traders said.
The current carrying charge for late May is 72.71 francs.
Time is running out for old-crop barley sales, with measures in force that would discourage EU exports from June onwards.
Riyadh wants the barley delivered by July 15.
"It's the Commission which holds the key," one French trader said after Friday's launch of the tender. "Will it do something even though there is a negative corrective of 20 Ecus in June?"
The corrective is deducted from export subsidies issued at a weekly tender and is a way of narrowing the flexibility of export licences normally valid for at least four months.
On Thursday the EU awarded subsidies up 15.90 Ecus a tonne for 89,200 tonnes of barley exports, meaning the licences must be used within two weeks to avoid effectively paying a tax.
Saudi Arabia launched a tender on Friday for 450,000 tonnes of optional-origin barley to be delivered to Jeddah, and another 250,000 tonnes to reach Dammam -- both by July 15.
Other potential suppliers include Australia, Canada and the United States, traders said.
